body:
**Tier:** T4 (re-graded upward in fix round 2, per the GPT-6.1 Sol release/native privacy lens: privacy policy for everything sent to Sentry, plus native code generation in AppDelegate.swift, MainApplication.kt and AndroidManifest.xml at prebuild)
**Why:** Sentry native auto-init is off: with `@sentry/react-native` 7.11 the native SDKs start only when `Sentry.init()` runs in JS (`src/services/sentry.ts`), so crashes during native module registration, JS bundle load or early bridge setup never reach Sentry (found in the 10-01 Android launch-crash hunt; the Crisp module crash was invisible).
**T4 trigger scan:** audited as T4 (privacy-relevant telemetry: the content policy for breadcrumbs, events and transactions, and the id-only user). No auth, payments, entitlement, migration, secret, or CI gate file.
**T3 trigger scan:** yes. Generated native code in both platforms' entry points, and the native fingerprint changes (new config plugin), so this needs a new binary.
**Bounded T1:** `src/hooks/README.md`.
**Builder-owner:** Claude Opus 5.5 (S-RELEASE-MOB, agent 112). Owner: operator. Needs an independent audit plus green CI, and a device check (below) before release.
**Acceptance evidence:** at 7d64054, the 7 targeted suites pass 123/123: the plugin, sentryPrivacy, sentry.payload (real SDK), sentry.privacy, useCurrentUser, expectedEnv and validateAppConfig. Against 4c61d91 the plugin and payload suites fail 14 of 28. tsc on the changed TS files is clean, and so is eslint. CI runs tsc and the full suites.
**Promotion triggers:** upgrading to `@sentry/react-native` 8 (`useNativeInit`), turning on native tracing or replay, or any change that sends user identity beyond the account id.

## What changes
- **`plugins/withSentryNativeInit.js`** (registered in app.json after the Sentry SDK plugins). The official `useNativeInit` option needs SDK 8, but Expo SDK 56 pins `@sentry/react-native ~7.11.0` (`expo/bundledNativeModules.json`). So the plugin starts the native SDKs 7.11 already ships, the same way SDK 8's `RNSentrySDK` does:
  - **iOS:** `import Sentry` and `SentrySDK.start { options in ... }` as the first statement of `application(_:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:)`, before the React Native factory exists. sentry-cocoa 8.58 is a dependency of the RNSentry pod (module `Sentry`).
  - **Android:** `SentryAndroid.init(this, Sentry.OptionsConfiguration<SentryAndroidOptions> { ... })` right after `super.onCreate()`, before `loadReactNative(this)`. `io.sentry:sentry-android:8.31.0` is an `api` dependency of the RN module.
  - When JS later calls `Sentry.init()`, the RN SDK re-initializes the native SDK with the JS options (`initNativeSdk`), so events after JS loads are unchanged.
- **Config (DSN from existing config):** `EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`, else `expo.extra.sentryDsn`. These are the same sources as `initSentry()`. Environment: `EXPO_PUBLIC_ENVIRONMENT` or `production`. Release: `<version>+<buildNumber|versionCode>`, which is the exact string `buildReleaseId()` reports, so pre-JS and post-JS crashes land in one release.
  - No DSN: nothing is added, so Sentry stays off, as in JS.
  - A DSN that is not `https://<key>@<host>/<id>` (a placeholder, or a value with quotes) fails prebuild. The DSN is never printed.
  - An unsafe environment or release fails prebuild.
  - A template the plugin cannot patch (anchor gone, Objective-C or Java entry file) fails prebuild instead of silently dropping native init.
  - Kill switch: `TGP_SENTRY_NATIVE_INIT=0` at build time.
- **No PII** (no health data, no message content):
  - **Native:** `sendDefaultPii=false`, no screenshots, no view hierarchy, no network breadcrumbs, no failed-request events (request URLs), no native performance tracing (JS owns tracing, which avoids duplicate transactions). No user exists before JS.
  - **JS `Sentry.init`:** the same flags (`sendDefaultPii`, `attachScreenshot`, `attachViewHierarchy`, `enableCaptureFailedRequests` all false).
  - **`setSentryUser`:** now sends `{ id }` only. It used to send the email, which also reached native crash reports through scope sync. `useCurrentUser` passes the id only.
- **Content policy at the JS boundary** (fix round 2, B-330-3). This is `src/services/sentryPrivacy.ts`, wired into `beforeBreadcrumb`, `beforeSend` and `beforeSendTransaction`. `sendDefaultPii: false` does not redact content, so this policy does.
  - Console breadcrumbs are dropped.
  - xhr, fetch and http breadcrumbs keep only the method, the status and a route-only URL:
    - no query, fragment or credentials;
    - any path segment that is not a plain lowercase word becomes `:id`.
  - Touch breadcrumbs keep component and file names, never labels.
  - Every other breadcrumb loses its message and any free text.
  - Events keep `user.id` only. Request bodies, cookies, query strings and the Authorization and Cookie headers are removed.
  - Transactions lose `http.query` and `http.fragment`. URL attributes and http.client span names are reduced to the route.
  - Native breadcrumbs that the RN SDK merges into JS events are scrubbed in `beforeSend`.
  - Scope sync copies JS breadcrumbs to native only after `beforeBreadcrumb`, so native crash reports carry the scrubbed versions.
- **Native suppression survives the JS re-init** (B-330-3).
  - **iOS:** `enableNetworkBreadcrumbs: false` and `enableNetworkTracking: false` are passed in the JS options. The RN SDK forwards every non-function option to `SentryOptionsInternal initWithDict` (sentry-cocoa 8.58 reads both keys).
  - **Android:** the plugin writes `io.sentry.breadcrumbs.network-events=false` into AndroidManifest. SentryAndroid applies manifest metadata on every `SentryAndroid.init`, including the RN SDK re-init, which has no option for it. It is set whatever the DSN, and has no effect when Sentry is off. Auto-init stays off: the RN module's manifest sets `io.sentry.auto-init=false`.
- **Prebuild reconciles** (B-330-4).
  - Every prebuild first removes the plugin-owned init block and import block, matching exact marker lines. They are re-added only when options resolve.
  - With the kill switch on or the DSN removed, an incrementally prebuilt file returns to the template byte for byte.
  - Imports the file already had outside the owned block are never touched. An unterminated block fails prebuild.
- **No dependency change** (package.json and package-lock.json untouched).

## Tests
```
heavy.sh npx jest --runInBand plugins/__tests__/withSentryNativeInit.test.js src/services/__tests__/sentry.privacy.test.ts src/hooks/__tests__/useCurrentUser.composition.test.tsx   -> 3 suites, 23 passed
heavy.sh npx jest --runInBand scripts/__tests__/expectedEnv.test.js scripts/__tests__/validateAppConfig.test.js   -> 69 passed
heavy.sh npx eslint <changed src + plugin files>   -> clean
```
The plugin tests run against the real Expo SDK 56 bare-minimum `AppDelegate.swift` and `MainApplication.kt` (fixtures copied from `expo/expo@sdk-56`). They check:
- placement: before the RN factory or `loadReactNative`
- every option line
- imports
- idempotency on a double prebuild
- that the template is otherwise unchanged
- loud failures
- DSN validation, including that the DSN is never printed
- release parity with the JS init
- plugin order in app.json

## Not proven here (device / build gate before release)
- iOS compile of `import Sentry` in the app target, and the Android compile. Prove these with one EAS preview build (operator-run). I did not build anything.
- **Device check:** force a crash before JS loads, then confirm it reaches Sentry on the next launch with release `1.0.0+<build>`, no user and no screenshot. Suggested method: a preview build with a temporary invalid bundle, or `adb shell am crash` during splash.
- Session counts can double-count at the native→JS re-init on iOS until SDK 8. This is release-health noise only.

Independent of mobile #305 (OTA). They touch different app.json keys (`plugins` vs `runtimeVersion`/`updates`), so either merge order is fine. This adds a config plugin, so it changes the native fingerprint, and binaries built before it cannot get it by OTA.

## Fix rounds
| Round | Head | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 5b987bf | — (initial) | — |
| 1 | 4c61d91 | CodeQL js/incomplete-sanitization ×2 (high): `.`-only RegExp escaping of import names (plugin:176, test:106) | Fixed: literal line comparison; no RegExp built from names |

### Fix round 2 (agent 112, S-RELEASE-2): merge of main f34b5b9 (6c8a02e), then fix commit 7d64054

| Finding | What changed | Commit | Test that proves it |
|---|---|---|---|
| B-330-3 (Sol): post-JS breadcrumbs and native re-init not covered | `sentryPrivacy.ts` policy on `beforeBreadcrumb` / `beforeSend` / `beforeSendTransaction`. iOS: native-only keys `enableNetworkBreadcrumbs` and `enableNetworkTracking` set false and forwarded to initWithDict. Android: `io.sentry.breadcrumbs.network-events=false` manifest flag (re-applied on every SentryAndroid.init) | 7d64054 | `src/services/__tests__/sentry.payload.test.ts`, which runs the **real @sentry/react-native 7.11 SDK** with only the native module doubled. The envelope sent to native carries no canary (JS xhr/fetch/console/free text, plus an iOS native http breadcrumb merged from device context) and no email. Scope-sync `addBreadcrumb` and `setUser` to native are scrubbed. `initNativeSdk` receives every privacy key. Also `sentryPrivacy.test.ts` (URL, breadcrumb, event and transaction canaries), `sentry.privacy.test.ts` › `wires the content policy into every send path (B-330-3)`, and `withSentryNativeInit.test.js` › `AndroidManifest network-events flag (B-330-3)` |
| B-330-4 (Sol): disabled prebuild keeps the old initializer | The registered appDelegate and mainApplication mods always reconcile: owned blocks are removed first and only re-added when options resolve. Imports are owned in a marked block | 7d64054 | `withSentryNativeInit.test.js` › `registered mods reconcile on every prebuild (B-330-4)`. It runs the actual registered mods enabled → disabled → enabled, for kill switch and DSN removal, on iOS and Android. Disabled output equals the SDK-56 template exactly, and re-enabled output equals the first enabled output. Also: pre-existing imports are kept, and an unterminated block throws |
| C-330-1 (Opus + Sol): README email example | `src/services/README.md`: `setSentryUser({id})` (account id only), and the policy is documented | 7d64054 | — (doc) |
| C-330-2 (Opus + Sol): device and server proof | **Deferred to the operator** (cannot be proven in the sandbox). Needed: one EAS preview build compiling `import Sentry` and the Kotlin block; a forced pre-JS crash reaching Sentry with release `1.0.0+<build>` and no user or screenshot; and the Sentry project setting "Prevent Storing of IP Addresses" on | — | — |
| Tier reconcile | Header changed from T3 to T4 | PR body | — |

**Local runs.**
- `heavy.sh env CI=true npx jest --runInBand --forceExit --runTestsByPath plugins/__tests__/withSentryNativeInit.test.js src/services/__tests__/sentryPrivacy.test.ts src/services/__tests__/sentry.payload.test.ts src/services/__tests__/sentry.privacy.test.ts src/hooks/__tests__/useCurrentUser.composition.test.tsx scripts/__tests__/expectedEnv.test.js scripts/__tests__/validateAppConfig.test.js`: 7 suites, **123/123**.
- The plugin and payload suites against 4c61d91's plugin and sentry.ts: **14 failed / 14 passed**.

**Sol probe** (`ops/aud-sol3-112/mobile330-independent-boundaries.test.js`) at 7d64054: 5/7.
- The 2 "remove DSN" cases fail because of a jest-expo harness artifact, not the plugin.
  - The probe reassigns `process.env = {...}` in `afterEach`.
  - babel-preset-expo rewrites the probe's static `process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` writes to its captured env object, so the plugin never sees the delete.
- With only those two env accesses changed to a computed key (`process.env[k]`), the same probe passes **7/7**. Real `expo prebuild` runs untransformed Node.
- The repo test sets and restores keys without reassigning `process.env`.

**Other checks.** eslint is clean. `check-expected-env`, `guard:vendors` and `validate:config` are OK.
title: feat(sentry): native crash capture before JS loads (iOS/Android), no PII
